extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 conflicting instructions evenly distributed between language and vision paradigms, designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is created using an automated framework called AutoCreate, which uses a small batch of manual seeds and Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate data. The process involves a Language Loop and a Visual Loop, where data is sequentially processed by a Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data consists of a small batch of manually input seeds for the generation loops, as well as external data from the ImageNet dataset for the SemanticConflict task.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is generated using an automatic framework called AutoCreate, which uses manually input seeds to generate data via LLMs (Generator, Decorator, Cleaner). Human experts and LLMs then double-check the quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality validation was performed by human experts rigorously checking the generated dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is currently limited to language-language and vision-language paradigms, and it lacks fine-grained control to determine the degree of conflict.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset provides a standardized platform to assess and improve how LMMs handle conflicting instructions, which promotes inclusivity in AI research and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems for societal integration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used as a benchmark for evaluating and testing Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) on their ability to detect and comprehend self-contradictory instructions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation is applied by varying image attributes (font, size, color) to increase diversity. Additionally, data sampling is used to create smaller subsets (10% and 1% of the full dataset) for different needs.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A cleaning step is employed where a 'Cleaner' module filters out generated data that fails to meet quality standards.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs). Specifically, in a single iteration, the generation process comprises two loops: the Language Loop (left) and the Visual Loop (right). Each loop originates from the Seed Pool and is sequentially processed by a fully automated Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner
